LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_EnableNewContent_Tooltip: New Hunger and Havoc incidents and visitors stop appearing. Visitors already here keep begging, trading, stealing, or leaving.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ResetConfirm: Restore all Ratkin: Hunger and Havoc settings to their defaults? Custom switches, values, and list selections will be reset. Story progress and visitors in your save remain unchanged.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Relief_Note: Visitors look for food they can reach inside the marked cells. Food outside, the limit after a meal, and leaving are set below.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ReliefEnabled_Tooltip: With this off, visitors ignore the marked cells. A zone already drawn stays on the map.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_EatOutsideRelief: Allow food outside the relief zone
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_EatOutsideRelief_Tooltip: With this off, visitors eat only food they can reach inside the zone. If the zone has none, they beg, wait, or leave.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_IgnoreReliefAfterFed: Ignore the relief zone after eating
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_IgnoreReliefAfterFed_Toolt: On, a full visitor may take the next meal from outside the zone. Off, a full visitor stops looking for another meal.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_LeaveAfterFed_Tooltip: On, a visitor who can reach an exit leaves after eating. An adult carries out a child too young or too weak to walk. Off, a full visitor stays on the map.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_MaxEventPawns_Tooltip: One incident stays at or under this count. 1 to 100, default 30. A lower count still uses that incident's minimum. A mother and child stay together.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ReliefScore_Tooltip: Food inside the zone adds this share of its distance and suitability score. 0 to 100%, default 10%.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FedWander_Tooltip: On, a full visitor wanders, then leaves. Off, they head for an exit at once. If leaving after eating is off, a full visitor stays on the map.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FedWanderHours_Tooltip: How long a full visitor wanders before leaving. 1 to 48 hours, default 12. Unused while wandering is off.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_WaitFood: Wait when no food is found
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_WaitFood_Tooltip: On, visitors keep looking for the set time. Finding food starts the next wait over. Off, they leave at once.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FoodWait_Tooltip: How long a visitor waits after finding nothing to eat. 0 to 5 days, default half a day.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_Age_Tooltip: Ordinary visitors arrive inside this range. 0 to 100, default 0 to 50. A mother stays at least as old as her own minimum. Ratkin young keep their own ages unless the switch below is on.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_YoungAge: Ratkin young use this age range
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_YoungAge_Tooltip: On, newly arriving ratkin young also use the range above. Off, begging young are 1 day to 2.9 years, and other young are 3 to 6.9. Mothers still use their own minimum age.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_MotherAge_Tooltip: A newly arriving mother or begging mother is at least this old. 1 to 14, default 14. If the ordinary arrival age is higher, that age wins. Ratkin young keep their own ages.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ImmobileBabies_Tooltip: Without a toddler mod, ratkin under 4 stay down, and an adult has to carry them out. Off, ratkin young arrive at least 4 years old.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ImmobileBabies_Toddlers: Toddlers is active. Children under 3 can move on their own. This switch no longer raises their age.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FemaleShare_Tooltip: Used only when gender is set by share. 0 is all male. 100 is all female. Someone whose gender the incident already set keeps it.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PlayerIdeo_Tooltip: This share of new arrivals, and of people who later join, takes the player faction's primary ideoligion. 100 converts all of them. 0 keeps the ideoligion they arrived with. With Ideology off, or with no primary ideoligion, nothing changes.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_Apparel_2: Plain clothes, then a temperature wrap
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_MaxTraits_Tooltip: A new visitor gains at most this many mod traits. 0 gives none. Range 0 to 3. People already here keep the traits they have.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_VanillaTraits_Tooltip: Off, new visitors gain no age-based vanilla traits. Mod traits still follow the limit above.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_TraitAge_Tooltip: Off, child traits and adult traits can both be chosen. On, children miss adult traits and adults miss child traits.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ShelterDays_Tooltip: A short-term worker leaves when the time is up. Minimum 5 days, maximum 1 year, default 5 days. A downed visitor stays on the map and resumes the remaining time after waking.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_HireDays_Tooltip: A long-term worker leaves when the time is up. Minimum 5 days, maximum 10 years, default 1 year. A downed visitor stays on the map and resumes the remaining time after waking.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ColdClothes: Give new visitors a temperature wrap
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ColdClothes_Tooltip: When the map is outside what a new visitor can bear, they get the lightest wrap that covers the gap. If none covers it, they get the thickest. Someone already wearing one keeps it. Off, no extra clothing is given.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_Temp_Tooltip: While the map is outside this range, new incidents aimed at the map stop. Default -35°C to 70°C. Caravans ignore this limit.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ReliefFoods_Tooltip: Visitors can take any food left on.
LanguageData.RHAH_ReliefArea_Expand_Desc: Mark cells where visitors may take food. An empty zone does not become the whole map.
LanguageData.RHAH_ReliefArea_Clear_Desc: Remove marked cells. Once none remain, visitors who cannot leave the zone stop taking food here.
LanguageData.RHAH_PlagueSpreading: Ratkin plague is spreading through the colony.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_Begging_Tooltip: Off, visitors stop begging from colonists.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BegAutoGive: Give carried food when begging succeeds
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BegAutoGive_Tooltip: Off by default. On, a successful beg takes one allowed food from the colonist's pack, highest nutrition first. Off, the visitor still asks, the food stays in the pack, and the beg does not count as success. Handing food over, relief food, and feeding during care continue as usual.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BegSuccessChance_Tooltip: Base chance the first time someone begs from one colonist. Social skill adds the bonus below, up to 100%. Default 35.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BegSocialBonus_Tooltip: Extra success chance for each level of the beggar's Social skill. 0 to 20, default 3. A later beg to the same colonist cannot succeed.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BegFoods_Tooltip: Food turned off stays in the pack when a beg succeeds. Raw food and ingredients are not on this list.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BegFoods_Quote: Food you turn off cannot be taken by begging. Meals added later can still be begged. Handing food over uses its own list.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BegFailCooldown_Tooltip: After every suitable colonist refuses, the visitor wanders this long before begging again. 3 to 12 hours, default 3.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BegSlapChance_Tooltip: The second time the same colonist is begged, and every time after, they may slap the beggar at this chance. 0 to 100, default 50.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_Fighting_Tooltip: Off, a harmed or driven-off visitor leaves instead of fighting back.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_Gnawing_Tooltip: Off, visitors stop gnawing bark or walls for food.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BatchHostile_Tooltip: Off, harming or driving off one visitor leaves the rest of that group as they are.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BatchLeave_Tooltip: Off, harm or expulsion affects only that visitor. The rest of the group stays.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ShortStayLockApparel: Lock current clothes for short stays
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ShortStayLockApparel_Toolt: On by default. Starting a short stay locks the clothes worn then. When the stay ends, or the visitor becomes a prisoner, slave, or colonist, only those locks come off. Off, a newly started short stay leaves clothes unlocked. A stay already underway keeps those clothes locked.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BroadcastCooldown_Tooltip: Days to wait after one broadcast before another. 0 to 10 days, default 3.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_RefugeeCamp_Tooltip: Off, temporary refugee camps stop appearing.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_Plague_Tooltip: Off, new visitors arrive healthy and the plague stops spreading through the colony. People already sick still need treatment.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PlaguePerCarrier_Tooltip: Each sick ratkin on the map adds this much chance that a colonist catches it. 0 to 100, default 0.5.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PlagueCap_Tooltip: One check gives a colonist at most this chance of catching it. 0 to 100, default 30.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PlagueDays_Tooltip: Days between spread checks. 1 to 30, default 3.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PlagueHour_Tooltip: The hour of day when spread is checked. 0 to 23, default 6.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PlagueBlood_Tooltip: A person at or above this blood pumping stays uninfected. 0 to 300, default 120.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PlagueReturn_Tooltip: Off, someone who left and recovered stays away.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PlagueDelay_Tooltip: After leaving and recovering, they return to the map edge after this many days. 0 to 60, default 15.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PlagueStay_Tooltip: A returned visitor leaves after this many days. 0 to 15, default 1.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_SuiyinTempo: Suiyin changes major threats with trust
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_SuiyinTempo_Tooltip: Off, major threats stay on their normal pace while Suiyin is the storyteller.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_Weight_Tooltip: Incidents of this kind are multiplied by this before one is chosen. 0 to 5. At 0, that kind stops appearing.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ReliefFoods_Quote: Visitors stop taking food you turn off. Food added later stays available.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_GiveFoods: Food that can be handed over
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_GiveFoods_Tooltip: Food turned off stays out of the right-click option for handing food to a visitor.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_GiveFoods_Quote: Food you turn off cannot be handed to visitors. Food added later can still be handed over.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_RefugeeApparel_Tooltip: Clothing you turn off is kept from new visitors. Temperature clothing is set on the environment page and worn first. Ordinary clothing is added only where it does not replace the wrap.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_RefugeeApparel_Quote: By default, visitors receive only vanilla tribalwear, the specified NewRatkinPlus clothes, and vanilla baby and child basics. Clothes from other mods stay off the default list. Ordinary clothes never replace a temperature wrap.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Environment_Note: When the map is outside what a new visitor can bear, they get the lightest wrap that covers the gap. If none covers it, they get the thickest. People already here keep the clothes they are wearing.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Environment_Disabled: Temperature wraps are off. New visitors get none of this extra clothing.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_TemperatureApparel_Tooltip: Off, new visitors get none of this wrap. Someone already wearing it keeps wearing it.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_TemperatureInsulation_Tool: Drag to set this wrap's protection. Range 0 to 100. At 0 it adds none of this protection.
LanguageData.RHAH_RemovalNoGame: Load a save before turning off its new content or exporting a copy for removal.
LanguageData.RHAH_RemovalDisable: Turn off new content for this save only
LanguageData.RHAH_RemovalDisabled: This save no longer starts new Hunger and Havoc content. Save once more before that state is in the original file. Visitors, letters, and places already here stay. The global switch is unchanged.
LanguageData.RHAH_RemovalExport: Back up and export a removal copy
LanguageData.RHAH_RemovalConfirm:
The game will pause. This save stops starting new content. A backup and a cleaned copy are saved. The original file is not overwritten.

The cleaned copy changes ratkin kinds, histories, hidden factions, and the storyteller. It removes this mod's traits, genes, health conditions, memories, items, zones, letters, and quests in progress. The people stay, and so does the ratkin mod.

After it succeeds, quit, remove only this mod, and keep the ratkin mod, Harmony, and Biotech. Restart and load the cleaned copy. The world still running is not cleaned. An unknown reference stops the export. Continue?
LanguageData.RHAH_RemovalFailed:
The cleaned export did not finish. Do not remove the mod because of it. New content for this save is already off.
Backup: {0}. If saving failed, that file may not exist.
Reason: {1}

The full error is in the log. The original file was not overwritten. The backup is not a cleaned copy.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Settings_Missing: Settings are not ready. Reopen this page and try again.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Events_Note: A checked incident can happen. Drag for a rough value, type the exact one. Scale changes how many people arrive and how much they ask for. At weight 0, it stops appearing.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_EventEnabled_Tip: Off, this incident stays out of the draw and cannot be queued from the dev mode page. Visitors already here stay as they are.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_DebugPoints_Tip: Natural incidents and dev mode triggers both use this size. It changes how many visitors arrive and how much aid or intel asks for. Range 1 to 10000. The slider is rough. The field is exact.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_IncidentWeight_Tip: 100 keeps the weight from the incident list. A higher weight appears more often. 0 stays out. The slider is rough. The field is exact.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Attitude_Tip: The five-step attitude used when this incident arrives. Leave it unchanged and the incident list decides. Under Suiyin, negative trust steps it down once. Hostile stays hostile. Visitors already here keep their attitude.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Chain_Tip: Short follow-up may send predators once this group appears. Long follow-up sends a later letter once the children reach the follow-up age, for incidents that have one. This still plays the incident once.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_TriggerInstant: Place them on this map now
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_TriggerInstant_Tip: Place them on the current map at once, skipping the queue and world travel. A caravan ambush places its attackers here. A refugee camp places its residents here. New content and incident switches still apply.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Instant_Failed: Nothing appeared. Check the incident switch, the map, and the log.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Queue_Queued: Queued. It appears when the pausing window closes.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_DevEvents_Note: Dev mode page. Queue the normal way and map visitors travel across the world first. Place them on this map now and they appear here without closing the window or sending a caravan.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Pawns_None: No Hunger and Havoc visitors on this map.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Narrative_NoGame: Narrative state needs a loaded game.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Ending_Gap: Ending switches are not available here yet.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Genes_Gap: Gene settings are not available here yet.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Genes_NoBiotech: Biotech is required. With it, you can set the xenotypes of visitors here.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Genes_Note: The percent is the chance while faster arrival is on. Weights run from 0 to 100. At 0, that xenotype stays out. Only ratkin xenotypes the race allows are listed. The base ratkin xenotype starts at a relative weight of 100 and stays in with the others. Each chance is its weight divided by the total. If every weight is 0, visitors use the allowed base ratkin xenotype, or the ratkin's own xenotype mix if that base is unavailable. An empty mix then tries the allowed famine ratkin xenotype. With faster arrival off, visitors use that mix directly. If no xenotype is available, visitor generation stops.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Genes_Fallback: The enabled weights add up to 0. Visitors use the allowed base ratkin xenotype, or the ratkin's own mix. If that is also empty, they try the allowed famine ratkin xenotype. If none of those is available, visitor generation stops.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Genes_WeightTip: Suggested weight {1}. Chance is this weight divided by the sum of enabled weights.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Genes_NoOwned: No Hunger and Havoc genes are available to toggle.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Genes_LitterMinTip: A birth has at least this many young. Range 1 to 12.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Genes_LitterPeakTip: This count is the most common. It stays between the minimum and the maximum.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Genes_LitterMaxTip: A birth has at most this many young. It cannot fall below the minimum.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Genes_FertileAgeTip: Both partners can conceive once they reach this age. Range 1 to 14.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Genes_FertilityTip: Pregnancy chance compared with normal. Range 100% to 1000%.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Genes_GestationTip: The shortest pregnancy is 3 days. It cannot run longer than the vanilla lower bound.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Genes_LovinPregnancyTip: Chance of pregnancy after lovin' finishes. Range 0% to 100%. Each partner's own pregnancy chance is still applied.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_PawnHistory_Note: New visitors take one checked history. Someone whose story the incident already wrote keeps that story. Traits can still be chosen.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_PawnHistory_ItemTip: Off, new visitors no longer receive this history. People already here keep the history they have.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_PawnTrait_ItemTip: Off, new visitors no longer receive this trait. People already here keep the trait they have.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_PawnTrait_WeightTip: A higher weight is chosen more often. 0 stays out. After it is chosen, weight divided by 100 is the chance they actually gain it. The slider is rough. The field is exact.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PawnHistories_Tooltip: Off, new visitors arrive without these histories. People already here keep the histories they have.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PawnTraits_Tooltip: Off, new visitors gain none of this mod's traits. People already here keep the traits they have. Each visitor still follows the limit above.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Experimental_Gap: This page only speeds up how visitors appear.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Experimental_Note: These options change how long visitors take to appear. With one off, visitors still arrive with that incident's own clothes, history, health, and genes.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_OptimizeGeneration_Tooltip: Visitors appear faster, with less random clothing and status. Without a set xenotype, the weights on the gene page decide.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Frequency_Gap: The line is the chance this group fires at least once on each coming day, from the average days above and the interval formula. Days run across. That day's chance runs up. 0 turns this group off. Rest the cursor on the line to read that day's chance. The graph uses the current trust and season.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Frequency_WindowTip: How many coming days the curve shows. 5 to 360. This only changes how many days are shown, not how often incidents fire.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Frequency_PaceTip: That day's average gap, in days. It can use the average days above (written as averageDays), day, trust, season, + - * /, parentheses, min, max, abs, and clamp. day is days since settling. season runs from 0 to 3. The result stays between 0 and 60. A bad formula, a division by 0, or an empty field uses the average days above. A result of 0 turns this group off.
LanguageData.RHAH_Menu_Developer_Note: Dev mode queues are on the trigger page. Version and IrisMenus are under Compatibility and diagnostics.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_AidRequests_Tooltip: Off, new aid and baby-exchange letters stop. An open request can still be delivered or refused.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_IntelTrades_Tooltip: Off, new intel stops being traded for a site. Sites already placed stay on the world.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_VisitorChoices_Tooltip: Off, new visitors stop asking to be taken in, hired, or sent away. The right-click menu still handles people already here.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FoodGiveHint_Tooltip: On, the first time you choose to feed them, the letter skips the explanation of how to hand the food over.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_TraderIgnoreEnvironment_To: On, famine traders stay after entering even in cold, heat, or dangerous weather. Off, harsh weather still sends them away.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_TraderIgnoreEnclosed: Trader caravans stay in closed rooms
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_TraderIgnoreEnclosed_Toolt: On, famine traders stay inside a closed room instead of digging out. Off, they dig out when they cannot reach the map edge.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_SpaceApproach_Tooltip: Off by default. Orbital homes, asteroids, and SOS2 ships then receive no ratkin who walk in, and map incidents stay out of the draw. Turn this on to allow both. A group already on an Odyssey orbit layer still leaves the shuttle launch clear.
LanguageData.RHAH_Approach_InterceptBlocked: Cannot intercept the Ratkin right now
LanguageData.RHAH_Approach_InterceptFailed: The interception map failed to generate. The Ratkin caravan is still where it was.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ChildExchangeFood: Allow food in place of children
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ChildExchangeFood_Tooltip: On, child exchange accepts simple meals instead of handing over a child. The cost follows Simple meals per child. Traders still sell no food. Off, this letter cannot be delivered, and handing over a child is not one of the choices either.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FamilyDrop_Tooltip: Off, a mother keeps carrying a child as she leaves.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_MotherFeed_Tooltip: Off, a mother keeps the meal in her pack instead of handing one to a hungry child.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PrisonerScavenge_Tooltip: Off, a hungry prisoner leaves the filth on the ground.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_TailBite_Tooltip: On, a hungry prisoner bites off the tail of a nearby sleeping prisoner under 3 who still has one. Off by default.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FamineDoors_Tooltip: Off by default. On, famine visitors may open colonist doors. They still leave doors shut while an enemy is on the map.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PlagueSafe_Tooltip: Off by default. On, the plague stops short of killing. The sick cannot move, but the plague itself leaves them alive.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_GreenLetters_Tooltip: On by default. Off, famine incident letters use the ordinary blue.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_Broadcast_Tooltip: Colonists can broadcast from a comms console and call famine ratkin here. Off, new broadcasts stop. Groups already on the road keep coming.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_Stagger_Tooltip: On, queued incidents arrive one batch at a time, with a short wait between them. Off, queued incidents arrive as soon as they can, one after another.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PredationChance_Tooltip: Each camp map rolls this chance for a predator. 0 to 100, default 10. At 0, none arrive.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PredationFightBack_Tooltip: Off, hunted camp ratkin run. Anyone who cannot use violence still cannot fight.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PredationFollowDifficulty: Outside predators hunt normally once the ratkin are gone
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PredationFollowDifficulty_: On, they resume ordinary hunting when no reachable ratkin or corpse remains. Off, a hungry predator with nothing reachable leaves the map.
LanguageData.RHAH_Predation_Text: A wild predator has started hunting these Ratkin refugees. It goes for the young first.
LanguageData.RHAH_OutsidePredators_Text: A predator followed the Ratkin refugees here and is looking for one it can eat.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Text: The visitors have stopped near the colony and stated their terms.\n\nThey want {1} {2}. What should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Aid_Text: A ratkin refugee has arrived near the colony, asking us for {1} {2}. There is plenty missing in a famine. This time, that is what they need.\n\nWhat should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Intel_Text: A ratkin has arrived near the colony with a lead on a place, willing to trade it for {1} {2}. The information is not free: goods first, directions afterward.\n\nDelivering the goods marks the corresponding site on the world map.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Baby_Text: A ratkin has arrived near our colony and asked us for a baby.\n\nWe can refuse or leave the request unanswered. If food substitution is enabled, we can hand over the required simple meals instead; a child cannot be handed over.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Abandoned_Text: A ratkin mother has left her children near our colony for reasons unknown. Perhaps she could no longer feed them, but could not bear to abandon them completely, so she brought them here. It seems she wants us to adopt them.\n\nThese young ratkin probably cannot survive on their own. What should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Refugees_Text: Ratkin refugees have arrived near our colony. The famine has driven them all the way here. They want to stay, somewhere they can find food and a place to sleep.\n\nWhat should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_ChildExchange_Text: A ratkin mother has brought a young ratkin near our colony. Before leaving, she says haltingly, "I really can't feed this child anymore, squeak. Could you give me some food? Or... could we make a trade?"\n\nShe wants food in exchange for her child. Or perhaps a different child who would count as 'food'. What should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Kinship_Text:
"Are you my mommy, squeak?"

"Squeak, squeak, squeak! You must be!"

"You're my mommy, squeak!"

A young ratkin has arrived near our colony, chattering away. Upon seeing a colonist, the child starts calling them Mommy in a strange, unclear little voice.

What should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Airdrop_Text: Someone has sent these young ratkin near our colony. We do not know who, or where they were meant to go. Left alone, they will probably starve. But taking them in also means finding enough food and people to care for them. Too many young ratkin may be more than the colony can manage. We should think carefully.\n\nWhat should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Visitors_Text: Ratkin visitors have arrived near our colony, with nowhere settled yet. Should we let them in, or let them keep walking?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_BeggarFamily_Text:
{0} has arrived.

Famine has driven a ratkin mother and her {1} children near our colony. She begs us for food while the young ratkin crowd around her feet.

"Please, squeak. Give me and my children some food."

She pauses. "We wouldn't complain even if you worked us like beasts."

What should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_LaboringRefugees_Text: {1} heavily pregnant ratkin have arrived near our colony, dragging their feet slowly. They have already gone into labor. Giving birth out in the wild is dangerous; it is hard not to worry whether the mothers and children will survive.\n\nWhat should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_PlagueAbandoned_Text:
The mother can barely stand. She pushes her child forward a little, then immediately reaches out to shield the child again.

"Help... help... my... child, squeak."

She never gives her name. Everything she could bring is left beside the child.

The mother has gone. The child is still here.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_ShatteredMother_Text: A ratkin mother has brought her children near our colony. She is badly injured and has lost a great deal of blood, with {1} children beside her.\n\nWhat should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_BeggarGroup_Text: Ratkin beggars have arrived near our colony, hoping for something to eat. The famine has driven them here, and their next meal is still uncertain.\n\nWhat should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Thieves_Text: Ratkin thieves have arrived near our colony. They are hungry too, but would rather take something edible than ask for a meal.\n\nHow should we deal with them?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_YoungThieves_Text: Young ratkin have arrived near our colony, learning to steal to fill their bellies. They are small, but hunger has already taught them to look for places with food.\n\nHow should we deal with them?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Wild_Text: Wild ratkin have wandered near our colony, without a caravan or anyone to speak for them. They are looking for food here.\n\nShould we take them in?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_WildYoung_Text: A wild young ratkin has wandered near our colony without an adult. There is food here, and people too, but not everything is safe.\n\nWhat should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Passersby_Text: A group of ratkin refugees is passing near our colony. They still need to find their next meal; passing through may not be all they do.\n\nShould we keep them here, or let them keep walking?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Siege_Text: Ratkin beggars have gathered around our colony. They want food, but do not act as though they are merely asking for a meal. Check whether they are hostile before deciding what to do.\n\nWhat should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Orphan_Text: A ratkin orphan has arrived near our colony without a mother. In this famine, one less adult means many fewer ways to stay alive.\n\nWhat should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_KinshipGrown_Text: A ratkin has arrived near our colony and started calling a colonist Mother. The colonist has never met this ratkin, but the visitor insists there is no mistake.\n\nWhat should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_VisitorHint: We have {0} days to answer. To arrange food delivery, select a colonist and right-click a visitor. If we refuse or the deadline passes, they will leave or turn hostile according to their attitude and the group reaction settings.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_RequestHint: We have {0} days to answer. If we refuse or the deadline passes, they will leave or turn hostile according to their attitude and the group reaction settings.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_IntelHint: We have {0} days to answer. The visitor will reveal the site after we deliver the goods. If we refuse or the deadline passes, they will leave or turn hostile according to their attitude and the group reaction settings.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_PlagueHint: These visitors carry the plague, and it may spread through the colony. Quarantine follows the current settings.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_PlagueDisabledHint: The plague is off. This group arrives healthy and skips quarantine.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_ChildExchangeFoodHint: We can fulfill this request with simple meals: {0} per child, {1} in total. A child cannot be handed over; taking the children into the colony requires a separate decision.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_ChildExchangeNoFoodHint: Food substitution is disabled, and a child cannot be handed over. We can refuse or leave the request unanswered.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_ChildExchangeZeroFoodHint: Meals per child is set to 0, so delivery is unavailable. To deliver meals, set the amount above 0; a child cannot be handed over.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_AbandonedGrown_Text: A ratkin mother has left her children near our colony for reasons unknown. Perhaps she could no longer feed them, but could not bear to abandon them completely, so she brought them here. It seems she wants us to take them in.\n\nWithout anyone looking out for them, they will probably struggle to survive. What should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_ChildExchangeGrown_Text: A ratkin mother has brought one of her children near our colony. Before leaving, she says haltingly, "I really can't feed my child anymore, squeak. Could you give me some food? Or... could we make a trade?"\n\nShe wants food in exchange for her child. Or perhaps a different child who would count as 'food'. What should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_BeggarFamilyGrown_Text:
{0} has arrived.

Famine has driven a ratkin mother and her {1} children near our colony. She begs us for food while they stand beside her.

"Please, squeak. Give me and my children some food."

She pauses. "We wouldn't complain even if you worked us like beasts."

What should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_AirdropGrown_Text: Someone has sent these ratkin near our colony. We do not know who, or where they were meant to go. Left alone, they will probably starve. But taking them in means finding enough food and shelter. Too many arrivals may be more than the colony can manage. We should think carefully.\n\nWhat should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_KinshipInfant_Text: A ratkin baby has been left near our colony. Too young even to say Mommy, the baby can only cry and wait for someone to help.\n\nWhat should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_AbandonedSingle_Text: A ratkin mother has left her child near our colony for reasons unknown. Perhaps she could no longer feed the young ratkin, but could not bear to abandon the child completely, so she brought the child here. It seems she wants us to adopt the child.\n\nThis young ratkin probably cannot survive alone. What should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_AbandonedSingleGrown_Text: A ratkin mother has left one of her children near our colony for reasons unknown. Perhaps she could no longer feed her child, but could not bear to abandon the child completely, so she brought the child here. It seems she wants us to take the child in.\n\nWithout anyone looking out for this ratkin, survival will probably be difficult. What should we do?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_WildSingle_Text: A wild ratkin has wandered near our colony, without a caravan or anyone to speak for them. The visitor is looking for food here.\n\nShould we take them in?
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Enslave: Enslave (become slaves where they stand, will cleared)
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Capture: Capture (become prisoners where they stand, asleep for 12 hours)
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_NoAlly: No allied faction can take them.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_AllySent: {0} people are on their way to {1} and will become members of that faction after leaving this map. They cannot be found directly at its settlement; goodwill changes depend on their treatment and whether they leave safely.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_NoCustodyTarget: No visitor can currently be captured or enslaved. They may be in a mental break, have already left, or be protected from imprisonment.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_NoPresent: The visitors have left. Nobody remains to receive this arrangement.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_NoRecruit: None of these visitors can be taken in, hired, or joined to the colony.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_NoTransfer: No visitor can currently be sent to an ally and leave the map.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_CustodyFailed: The attempt to capture or enslave the visitors failed. You can choose again in the letter.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_FeedHint: The visitors will wait for you to arrange food delivery. Select a colonist, then right-click a waiting visitor and choose the food to give them.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_FeedNoVisitor: {0} is not one of the visitors you can feed.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Short: Storage is short. They still need {0}.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_NoBaby: A child cannot be handed over this time. To use simple meals instead, turn food substitution on, set meals per child above 0, and have enough simple meals.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Stale: This letter can no longer take that choice.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_Delivered: The goods have been handed over.
LanguageData.RHAH_Choice_SiteUnavailable: The visitor could not provide a site. You still have the goods and can choose again in the letter.
LanguageData.RHAH_Intel_Text: The trade is done. A site has appeared nearby.
LanguageData.RHAH_Broadcast_Cooldown: The broadcast is still cooling down
LanguageData.RHAH_Broadcast_Queued: The broadcast has been sent. Waiting for ratkin to respond.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_EndingFloor_Tooltip: Minimum trust for "A year of plenty". Range 0 to 100, default 50. The trust requirement for "City of hope" is at least this high.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_EndingHope_Tooltip: Minimum trust for "City of hope", at least as high as for "A year of plenty" and at most 100. Default 75.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_EndingHalt_Tooltip: When Suiyin's trust falls to this value or lower, "The record stops" can occur. Range -100 to 0, default -75.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_EndingKinds_Tooltip: At least this many kinds of incidents must be completed successfully before "An unanswered record" or "A disappointed witness" can occur. Range 1 to 14, default 6.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_EndingThreat_Tooltip: Base interval between Suiyin's major threats. Higher trust lengthens the interval; lower trust shortens it. Range 1 to 60 days, default 13 days.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeKinds_Tooltip: Suiyin sends this letter after you have experienced at least this many kinds of incidents. Range 1 to 14.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeTheft_Tooltip: A grain hole can appear after this many thefts at one colony. Range 1 to 14 thefts, default 2.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeSilver_Tooltip: Base amount of silver Suiyin sends with the record letter. If her trust in you is above 0, she adds more silver in proportion to her trust. Range 0 to 10000, default 300.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeBonus_Tooltip: At trust 100, Suiyin adds this percentage of the base silver amount. Between trust 0 and 100, the bonus is reduced proportionally. Range 0 to 100%, default 25%.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeRescue_Tooltip: Silver paid to keep the banished mother or child. 0 to 10000, default 250.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeRescueReward_Tool: Silver dropped later after the ransom is paid. 0 to 20000, default 2500.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeTake_Tooltip: Silver gained by taking the migration record. 0 to 10000, default 200.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeHand_Tooltip: Silver gained by handing the migration record over. 0 to 10000, default 100.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeCare_Tooltip: Visitors count as settled after accumulating this many days at the colony while fed and free of plague. Range 0 to 120 days, default 5 days.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeMissing_Tooltip: Suiyin considers a visitor missing after this many days without knowing their whereabouts. Range 0 to 60 days, default 1 day.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeObserve_Tooltip: Suiyin waits up to this many days to learn the outcome of aid and entrusted children. If the visitors remain unsettled by the deadline, the aid does not count as successful. Range 0 to 120 days, default 30 days.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeHole_Tooltip: If you leave a grain hole alone, it disappears after this many days and the trail is lost. Range 0 to 30 days, default 3 days.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeEnvoyWait_Tooltip: The envoy waits up to this many days. If you leave the request unanswered, he leaves. Range 0 to 30 days, default 3 days.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeEnvoyCheck_Toolti: After you agree to check the envoy's account, he waits this many more days. Range 0 to 30 days, default 1 day.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeRelicDays_Tooltip: The migration record site remains available for this many days, then disappears from the world map. Range 0 to 120 days, default 15 days.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeReturn_Tooltip: Visitors can return this many days after recovering and leaving quarantine. Range 0 to 120 days, default 15 days.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeYears_Tooltip: After a mother or child is banished, a caravan may encounter them again within this many years. Range 0 to 20 years, default 4. A year is 60 days.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeAside_Tooltip: Minimum interval between Suiyin's short notes. Range 0 to 30 days, default 3 days.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeCutoff_Tooltip: When Suiyin's trust falls to this value or lower, she stops sending short notes but still sends incident outcomes. Range -100 to 0, default -75.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_NarrativeAdult_Tooltip: Age of the envoy Suiyin sends. Range 1 to 80 years, default 18.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_TrustRange_Tooltip: Amount added to or subtracted from Suiyin's trust in you when this happens. Range -100 to 100; at 0, trust stays unchanged.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BegFailMood_Tooltip: Mood after a refused beg. -50 to 50, default -5.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BegSuccessMood_Tooltip: Mood after a successful beg. -50 to 50, default 3.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BegSlapMood_Tooltip: Mood after a slap for begging again. -50 to 50, default -10.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BegKnock_Tooltip: Hours a slap stuns the beggar. 1 to 24 uses that many hours. 0 is the default and stuns for half an hour.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BegBruise_Tooltip: Severity of the first bruise. 0 to 40, default 4.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BegBruiseStep_Tooltip: Severity added by another slap on the same bruise. 0 to 40, default 4.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_BegBruiseMax_Tooltip: A bruise at this severity becomes a cut. It cannot sit below the first hit. Up to 40, default 16.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_GnawBark_Tooltip: Nutrition from one bite of a plant. 0 to 2, default 0.25.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_GnawBarkDamage_Tooltip: Fixed hit points removed by one bite of a plant. Material, building, and damage multipliers do not change the bite. 0 to 50, default 12.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_GnawWall_Tooltip: Nutrition from one bite of a wall. 0 to 2, default 0.20.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_GnawWallDamage_Tooltip: Fixed hit points removed by one bite of a wall. Material, building, and damage multipliers do not change the bite. 0 to 50, default 10.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ClayBites_Tooltip: Bites of clay allowed in one window. 0 to 12, default 3. Zero allows none.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ClayDays_Tooltip: Days before the bite count starts over. 1 to 60, default 15.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ClaySeverity_Tooltip: Fullness added by one bite. 0 to 1, default 0.33.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ChildHungry_Tooltip: A mother feeds a child below this food level. 0 to 100, default 30.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PrisonerHungry_Tooltip: A prisoner scavenges or bites a tail below this food level. 0 to 100, default 20.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_TailAge_Tooltip: Only a sleeping child under this age can be bitten. 0 to 18, default 3.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_Scavenge_Tooltip: Nutrition from licking filth once. 0 to 2, default 0.15.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_TailFood_Tooltip: Nutrition from a successful tail bite. 0 to 2, default 0.35.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_TailFail_Tooltip: Damage when the bite does not take the tail. 0 to 50, default 4.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FoodFull_Tooltip: Food at or above this counts as fed. 1 to 100, default 82.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FoodRefeed_Tooltip: Fed visitors look for food again at this malnutrition. 0 to 1, default 0.40.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_PlagueSeverity_Tooltip: Highest severity a new infection can reach. 0.01 to 1, default 0.10.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FollowPredator_Tooltip: When an incident uses the short follow-up, this is the chance predators are sent once that group appears. 0 to 100, default 10. At 0, none are sent.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FollowBirth_Tooltip: Days after a laboring birth before the mood is written. 0 to 60, default 3.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FollowPlagueBirth_Tooltip: Days after a plague birth before the mood is written. 0 to 60, default 5.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FollowMother_Tooltip: Days before a plague mother comes back. 0 to 120, default 15.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FollowYears_Tooltip: When an incident with a follow-up uses the long one, the letter waits at most this many years after the children reach the follow-up age. 0 to 20, default 2. The mother's return uses its own day count.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FollowAdult_Tooltip: Age used by the long follow-up and its later mood. 1 to 80, default 14.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FollowMood_Tooltip: Scales the later mood by this much. 0 to 300, default 100. A result under 1 point still leaves 1 point in the original direction.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_RequestRange_Tooltip: Minimum or maximum for this request. Wealth still picks a count inside the range.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_RequestDays_Tooltip: Days before an aid or intel letter expires. 0 to 30, default 1. Zero expires as soon as it arrives.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_RequestPoints_Tooltip: Requests scale against this point value. 1 to 10000, default 300.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FoodPerChild_Tooltip: Simple meals that replace one child. 0 to 100, default 10.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FoodPerVisitor_Tooltip: Portions requested per visitor when feeding them. 0 to 20, default 1.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_FoodRequestCap_Tooltip: Most portions one feeding request can ask for. 0 to 100, default 12.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_EnvoyMeals_Tooltip: Simple meals required to trade with the envoy. 0 to 100, default 6.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_CampRange_Tooltip: Minimum or maximum people in a camp of this age.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_CampGoodwill_Tooltip: Goodwill for clearing a camp. -100 to 100, default 12.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_CampDays_Tooltip: Days a camp quest lasts. 1 to 120, default 15.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_CampHuts_Tooltip: Huts placed in a camp. 0 to 12, default 4.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_HoleWood_Tooltip: Wood required to seal a grain hole. 0 to 200, default 20.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_HoleClean_Tooltip: Food portions removed when a grain hole is cleared. 0 to 50, default 5.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_HoleRange_Tooltip: Tiles from the hole that food can be taken. 1 to 60, default 12.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_HoleLosses_Tooltip: Most losses while a grain hole is left alone. 0 to 20, default 3.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ApparelAwful_Tooltip: Chance a new visitor wears awful clothes. The rest is poor, then normal. 0 to 100, default 35.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ApparelPoor_Tooltip: Chance of poor clothes. Awful and poor together cannot pass 100. Default 50.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ApparelDurability_Tooltip: Durability percent of new clothes. The minimum cannot pass the maximum. 1 to 100.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ApparelCorpse_Tooltip: Chance new clothes were worn by a corpse. 0 to 100, default 25.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ApparelCloth_Tooltip: Chance of cloth when both cloth and human leather are allowed. The rest is human leather. 0 to 100, default 65.
LanguageData.RHAH_Settings_ApparelPieces_Tooltip: Most pieces one adult visitor wears. 1 to 8, default 4.
